svg.title: QTFY QScan and QTRouter kill chain - scanning, exploitation, relay and seizure
svg.desc: Two-lane kill chain. Left lane, what a targeted organisation sees: 1 exposed edge service scanned by QScan workers, 2 exploitation of one of 14 KEV-listed CVEs, 3 foothold by web shell, RAT or valid account, 4 operator traffic arriving from nearby compromised devices through QTRouter, 5 assessed follow-on lateral movement and collection, 6 detection anchors that survive the takedown, 7 the 2026-08-26 domain seizure and residual risk. Right lane, the QTFY platform: A the Nanjing Xinjiuwei operator and customers, B QScan RabbitMQ and Redis scanning fleet, C QTRouter on OpenWrt with Clash, D Fast Labyrinth and QTProxy relay layer, E botnet management platforms and binaries, F resale and the DoJ seizure of qtproxy.xyz, qt-proxy.org and qt-team.com. Critical stages are shown in red.
svg.text: QTFY: QScan + QTRouter state-enabling relay platform
Vendor: FBI/NSA/CNMF + Lumen + DoJ - Date: 2026-08-26 - Cluster: QTFY (QT, QTCYBER) - Day 110
TARGETED ORGANISATION (what defenders see)
QTFY PLATFORM (operator side)
Edge service scanned by QScan workers
Rotating /24 worker blocks hit exposed VPN, web and file
transfer services; scanning looks like background noise
Worker lifecycle is about 30 days, so lists go stale fast
T1595.002 Vulnerability Scanning
src: leased servers, mostly outside China
Exploitation of an edge product CVE
14 CVEs named, all on CISA KEV: Pulse, Fortinet, Citrix,
Exchange, F5, Kentico, Log4j, Confluence, Check Point,
Ivanti CSA, CrushFTP, BeyondTrust
T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application
Foothold: web shell, RAT or valid account
Persistence through web shells, remote access trojans
and legitimate credentials on the compromised service
Scripts appear under web roots outside change windows
T1505.003 Web Shell T1078 Valid Accounts
hunt: new .aspx .jsp .php under web roots
Operator access via nearby compromised devices
Traffic reaches the victim from IoT devices in its own
region, chained through QTRouter and commercial proxies
Source blocking and geofencing fail against this design
T1090.003 Multi-hop Proxy
hunt: first-seen ASN logins, edge egress
Follow-on activity (assessed by Lumen)
Bidirectional contact with QScan targets likely means
attempted exploitation, lateral movement, persistent
access or data collection against high-value networks
assessed, not proven per intrusion
targets: defense, gov, universities, energy
Detection anchors that survive the takedown
12 months of DNS and flow history for the seized domains
Edge appliance egress to unexpected destinations
Hashes and names of agent_linux_*, client_linux_*
Sigma x3 KQL x3 YARA x2 Suricata x11
H1 retro hunt H2 edge hunt H3 ORB hunt
Seizure 2026-08-26 and residual risk
DoJ seized the hard-coded domains; both platforms stop
Compromised devices and past intrusions remain
Re-image relay devices; patch KEV-listed edge products
qtproxy.xyz qt-proxy.org qt-team.com
Lumen null-routed known operator infrastructure
A
Operator: Nanjing Xinjiuwei (XJW) as QTFY
Aliases QT and QTCYBER; active since at least May 2018
Court filing: former PLA members, payments from the MSS
Customers named: MSS and PLA; access also resold
confidence: high (platform), low (per intrusion)
advisory JCSA-20260826-01, revised 2026-09-02
B
QScan: distributed scanning and exploitation
RabbitMQ task broker mq-task hands jobs to workers
Redis collector mq-result stores completed tasks
200+ Python proof-of-concept exploits for scale
mq-task 154.64.238.222 mq-result .247
mq-task/mq-result.qt-proxy.org (was qt-team.com)
C
QTRouter: obfuscation network on OpenWrt
Custom OpenWrt routers, commercial proxy IPs, Alibaba
Cloud IPs and compromised IoT devices as relay nodes
Clash client chains nodes to hide the operator
www.qtproxy.xyz -> 1.32.216.171
securelink.qtproxy.xyz jump.qt-proxy.org
D
Fast Labyrinth and QTProxy relay layer
Encrypted relay on commercial fastlink.ws nodes
QTProxy control plane selects relays and custom paths
V2Ray, Shadowsocks and Trojan protocols (Airport style)
egress: flanycast-* / flnode-* .yotocloud.com
Go-http-client logins against www.qtproxy.xyz
E
Botnet management platforms and binaries
Proxy Platform Management, Proxy Pool Management and
QTBotnet: controller, secondary servers, infected nodes
Can launch DDoS and run commands on nodes
agent_linux_* client_linux_* c_client_* x45 hashes
scripts a b c d e f in.sh
F
Resale and the DoJ seizure
QScan and QTRouter access sold to other actors to hit
IoT devices that become more botnet nodes
Seized domains were hard-coded, so tools went inoperable
DoJ release 26-972, S.D. Cal., 2026-08-26
FBI SD + Cyber Division, NSA, CNMF, Lumen
Detection anchors (historical after seizure): DNS and flow to the QTFY domain set, QScan worker probing, edge egress, agent_linux hashes
Rules in this folder: Sigma 01-03, KQL k1-k3, YARA qtfy_qscan_qtrouter.yar, Suricata sids 6270001-6270011, PEAK hunts H1-H3.
Indicators decay: worker /24 blocks rotate about every 30 days and seized domains no longer reach operator infrastructure.
All 14 advisory CVEs are on CISA KEV. Sources: FBI/NSA/CNMF advisory, DoJ 26-972, Lumen Black Lotus Labs (2026-08-26).
